subject: Creativity
title: Reading Fiction: Imagination Gym for Empathy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Reading Fiction: Imagination Gym for Empathy.

hook.text: Reading fiction makes you a better mind-reader. Studies show fiction readers score higher on empathy and social.

buildup.text: When you read a novel, your brain simulates the characters' experiences — running their emotions through your own.

discovery.text: Literary fiction — which emphasizes complex, ambiguous characters — produces stronger empathy gains than genre fiction.

twist.text: Experiments suggest literary fiction can briefly sharpen empathy and perspective-taking.

climax.text: A lifetime of reading is a lifetime of practice at imagining what it's like to be someone else.

punchline.text: Every novel you read trains your brain to understand other minds.

quiz.question: Which type of fiction produces the strongest empathy improvements?
